Frequentist Network Meta-Analysis in Oncology: From 5 Lines of Code to Top-Tier Publication

First-Line Systemic Therapies for Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) - Overall Survival

Elite Biostatistics & Evidence Synthesis Portfolio

2026-09-18

R 4.6.1 netmeta v3.6 PRISMA-NMA Compliant High-Impact Medical Standard

1 Executive Summary & Philosophical Hook

1.1 English Executive Summary

Why Start with Frequentist Network Meta-Analysis?

Because within 5 lines of R code, an investigator can build a complete evidence network, execute indirect treatment comparisons, and generate a publication-ready League Table. This allows researchers and clinicians to grasp the fundamental mechanics of indirect evidence synthesis and transitivity before confronting the computational overhead and prior sensitivity of Bayesian MCMC modeling.

This report presents a comprehensive, publication-grade Network Meta-Analysis (NMA) adhering to the PRISMA-NMA reporting guidelines and formatted to meet the editorial standards of high-impact medical journals (The Lancet, BMJ, JAMA, NEJM).

1.1.1 Clinical Scope

  • Indication: First-line systemic therapy for advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC).
  • Primary Endpoint: Overall Survival (OS) quantified as Hazard Ratios (\(\text{HR}\)) with \(95\%\) Confidence Intervals.
  • Evidence Base: 24 Randomized Controlled Trials (15,753 patients), including 20 two-arm trials and 4 three-arm multi-center Phase III trials.
  • Regimens Evaluated:
    1. Chemo: Platinum-doublet Chemotherapy (Historical Standard Reference).
    2. IO_Mono: Anti-PD-(L)1 Monotherapy (e.g., Pembrolizumab, Atezolizumab).
    3. IO_Chemo: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor + Platinum Chemotherapy.
    4. Dual_IO: Dual Checkpoint Blockade (Anti-PD-1 + Anti-CTLA-4).
    5. TKI: Targeted Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Monotherapy (EGFR/ALK).
    6. TKI_Chemo: Targeted Therapy + Platinum Chemotherapy combination.

1.2 الملخص التنفيذي بالعربية

لماذا تبدأ بالتحليل التلوي الشبكي التكراري (Frequentist NMA)؟

لأنك تستطيع كتابة 5 أسطر برمجية فقط في R والحصول فوراً على شبكة متكاملة وجداول مقارنة ثنائية (League Tables)، وتفهم منها المعنى الرياضي والسريري الحقيقي لـ “المقارنة غير المباشرة” (Indirect Comparison) دون الغوص أولاً في تعقيدات الرياضيات البايزية ومحاكاة سلاسل ماركوف مونت كارلو (MCMC).

أهم ما يبرزه هذا التقرير:

  1. تنظيم بيانات البقاء المقارنة: تحويل قيم معدل الخطر (\(\text{HR}\)) وفترات الثقة إلى لوغاريتم معدل الخطر \(\ln(\text{HR})\) والخطأ المعياري \(\text{seTE}\).
  2. المعالجة الرياضية الدقيقة للدراسات متعددة الأذرع (Multi-arm trials): الحفاظ على التباين المشترك الموجب (Positive-definite covariance matrix) واتساق التباينات.
  3. ترتيب الفاعلية عبر مقياس P-score: المعادل التكراري لـ SUCRA البايزي لتقييم احتمالية تفوق كل علاج.
  4. فحص فرضية الاتساق (Inconsistency Evaluation): تفكيك إحصائية \(Q\) العالمية لشرح التباين داخل وخارج التصاميم، واختبار شطر العقد المحلي (Node-splitting) للكشف عن أي خلاف بين الأدلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة.

2 Mathematical Foundations of Network Meta-Analysis

2.1 Contrast Data Representation for Survival Outcomes

In time-to-event outcomes (Overall Survival, Progression-Free Survival), clinical trials report Hazard Ratios (\(\text{HR}\)) and \(95\%\) Confidence Intervals \([\text{lower}, \text{upper}]\). Because the distribution of \(\text{HR}\) is right-skewed, synthesis is conducted on the natural logarithmic scale:

\[\text{Treatment Effect } (y_i) = \text{TE}_i = \ln(\text{HR}_i)\]

The standard error (\(\text{seTE}_i\)) is derived from the symmetrical Gaussian limits:

\[\text{seTE}_i = \frac{\ln(\text{upper}_i) - \ln(\text{lower}_i)}{2 \times 1.95996}\]

2.2 Bucher’s Principle of Indirect Comparison

For any three treatments \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\), where direct trials exist for \(A \text{ vs } B\) and \(A \text{ vs } C\), but no direct trials have compared \(B \text{ vs } C\):

\[\ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{BC}^{\text{indirect}}) = \ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{AC}^{\text{direct}}) - \ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{AB}^{\text{direct}})\]

Under independence, the variance of this indirect contrast is simply additive:

\[\text{Var}\left(\ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{BC}^{\text{indirect}})\right) = \text{Var}\left(\ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{AC}^{\text{direct}})\right) + \text{Var}\left(\ln(\widehat{\text{HR}}_{AB}^{\text{direct}})\right)\]

2.3 Graph-Theoretical Synthesis (G. Rücker Electrical Network Model)

netmeta generalizes Bucher’s method to complex networks with multiple loops, active controls, and multi-arm trials using graph theory. The evidence network is represented as an electrical circuit where: - Nodes represent treatments. - Conductances (\(w_{ij} = 1/\text{Var}_{ij}\)) represent the precision of direct head-to-head evidence. - The Laplacian matrix \(L\) combines the network topology and weights:

\[L_{ij} = \begin{cases} -w_{ij} & \text{if } i \neq j \\ \sum_{k \neq i} w_{ik} & \text{if } i = j \end{cases}\]

The Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse \(L^+\) provides the combined treatment estimates and their standard errors across all closed loops simultaneously.

3 The 5-Line Pedagogical Quickstart

The entire analysis can be initiated in 5 lines of R code:

# Line 1: Load netmeta package
library(netmeta)

# Line 2: Read contrast dataset
dat <- read.csv("../data/nsclc_trial_contrasts.csv")

# Line 3: Fit NMA model
nma <- netmeta(TE, seTE, treat1, treat2, studlab, data = dat, sm = "HR", ref = "Chemo")

# Line 4: Generate Network Graph
netgraph(nma, points = TRUE, col = "#2b6cb0", plastic = FALSE, thickness = "number.of.studies")

# Line 5: View League Table (Random-Effects)
knitr::kable(netleague(nma, digits = 2)$random, caption = "Pairwise League Table (Random-Effects)")

4 Evidence Network Geometry

The geometry plot displays the topology of the clinical evidence base. Node diameters reflect total patient enrollment, line thickness reflects the volume of direct trial comparisons, and shaded polygons indicate multi-arm studies.

5 Comparative Efficacy vs Standard Reference (Chemo)

The forest plot displays the relative survival benefit of all active regimens compared to standard Platinum Chemotherapy (Chemo), sorted by clinical hierarchy.

6 Treatment Ranking Hierarchy (P-Scores)

The frequentist P-score measures the certainty that one treatment is superior to another, averaged across all competing interventions. It is mathematically equivalent to the Bayesian Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking (SUCRA) curve:

\[P\text{-score}_i = \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{j \neq i} \Phi\left(\frac{\widehat{\theta}_i - \widehat{\theta}_j}{\sqrt{\text{Var}(\widehat{\theta}_i - \widehat{\theta}_j)}}\right)\]

8 Methodological Assumption Testing: Inconsistency & Transitivity

Network Meta-Analysis rests on the transitivity assumption (that anchor treatments are clinically similar across trial loops). Inconsistency occurs if direct and indirect evidence are discordant.

8.1 Global Inconsistency Decomposition (Cochran’s \(Q\))

Total network variance \(Q\) is decomposed into within-design heterogeneity (\(Q_{\text{het}}\)) and between-design inconsistency (\(Q_{\text{inc}}\)):

\[Q = Q_{\text{het}} + Q_{\text{inc}}\]

Table: Global Test of Heterogeneity and Inconsistency
Component Q Statistic Degrees of Freedom p-value Clinical Interpretation
Total Variation (Q) 21.44 23 0.5544 No significant total excess variance
Within-Designs Heterogeneity (Q_het) 17.25 15 0.3043 Homogeneity within trial designs
Between-Designs Inconsistency (Q_inc) 4.19 8 0.8396 Full Transitivity/Consistency upheld

Result: The between-designs inconsistency test yields \(p = 0.8396\), confirming that the transitivity assumption is strictly upheld across the evidence network.

8.2 Local Inconsistency via Node-Splitting (Separating Direct from Indirect)

Node-splitting separates direct evidence from indirect evidence for every closed loop in the network. A \(p\)-value \(< 0.05\) flags local inconsistency.

8.3 Net Heat Plot (Inconsistency Hot-Spots)

The Net Heat plot identifies which specific trial designs drive instability or introduce tension into the network estimates.

9 Small-Study Effects & Publication Bias

To evaluate whether smaller trials systematically report exaggerated treatment effects, a comparison-adjusted funnel plot is generated, ordering treatments by their established clinical hierarchy.

Interpretation: The funnel plot displays symmetrical dispersion around the zero-line with no signs of small-study bias (\(p > 0.10\)).
